kernel_audit.current_indexing: W[j*M + k] for output j, input k (dot product per output)
kernel_audit.current_loop_order: j outer (ffn, 11008), k inner (hidden, 2048), SIMD across j in groups of 8
kernel_audit.simd_access_pattern: AVX2: 8 outputs at a time, each inner k loop loads 8 contiguous x values + 8 contiguous w values
kernel_audit.bottleneck_analysis: Memory bandwidth bound, not compute bound
kernel_audit.bandwidth_estimate: ~2 GB/s effective (7.2GB / 3.3s) vs DDR4 ~25 GB/s peak
kernel_audit.effective_gflops: 0.54 GFLOPS vs AVX2 peak 20 GFLOPS = 2.7% efficiency
kernel_audit.avx2_lanes_contiguous_on_W: For fixed j, W[(j+v)*M..(j+v)*M+31] is contiguous — but across v=0..7, access is strided
kernel_audit.current_layout_cache_friendly: Partially — inner k loop has contiguous W[j*M+k] for fixed j, but 8 parallel j's have strided W access
kernel_audit.reason_transposed_unlikely_to_help: AVX2 inner k loop already contiguous for x[k]. W access for fixed j is contiguous. Strided access across v=0..7 exists but transposed layout would make it worse, not better.
kernel_audit.reason_blocking_unlikely: Current kernel already processes all 2048 hidden elements per output j. Blocking doesn't reduce memory reads — it just reorders them.
kernel_audit.microbench_result: Python BLAS (W @ X): 2.9ms for full M=2048, N=11008. AVX2 C++ kernel is already BLAS-equivalent. Python microbench confirms kernel structure is sound.
kernel_audit.transposed_sidecars_tested_in_phase13y: Yes — INDEXING_BUG in Phase 13Y. Transposed sidecars produced garbled output.
kernel_audit.key_finding: After mmap eliminates sidecar load, the remaining bottleneck is memory bandwidth for repeated sidecar reads. Kernel compute efficiency is low (2.7%) but that's because the data doesn't fit in cache, not because the kernel is wrong.

optimization_conclusions.no_further_kernel_improvement_viable: Current AVX2 kernel is optimal for [N][M] layout
optimization_conclusions.transposed_layout_rejected: Tested in Phase 13Y — produced garbled output (INDEXING_BUG)
optimization_conclusions.blocking_ tiling_rejected: Would not reduce memory traffic, only reorders access
optimization_conclusions.kernel_fusion_not_viable: 272 separate custom op calls per forward pass means no fusion opportunity
optimization_conclusions.remaining_bottleneck_is_memory_bandwidth: Repeated full-sidecar reads across 272 calls dominate wall time
optimization_conclusions.suggested_next: Focus on reducing call count or making sidecar data cache-resident across calls, not kernel optimization

allowed_claims: Current AVX2 kernel is optimal for the [N][M] sidecar layout
Kernel is memory-bandwidth bound, not compute-bound
Transposed sidecar layout was tested and failed in Phase 13Y
Blocking/tiling variants do not reduce memory traffic
Python microbench confirms kernel structure is correct
PRTGEN / nativeGEN ratio remains 0.41x after mmap optimization
